findings.title: Interpolating before the split check drops the $__range exclusion
findings.body: runSplitQuery now runs every target through datasource.applyTemplateVariables before querySupportsSplitting. That helper substitutes variables via templateSrv.replace (the new test depends on this for both expr and step), and panel/Explore requests put __range, __range_s, and __range_ms on request.scopedVars. After substitution, isQueryWithRangeVariable no longer sees [$__range] / [$__range_s] / [$__range_ms], so a query such as count_over_time({app="foo"}[$__range]) is treated as splittable. The comment on querySupportsSplitting says these must not be split because the backend interpolates $__range from the time range of the request it actually receives. Each chunk is then executed with the full dashboard duration already baked in (or, if a later pass still sees the variable, with the chunk duration), so rates and range aggregations over multi-day windows are wrong or rejected by Loki. Keep the range-variable check on the pre-interpolation expression, and add a regression test that a $__range query is not split.

findings.title: Shard path applies template variables twice
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery now maps every target through applyTemplateVariables(query, scopedVars, request.filters) and then splitQueriesByStreamShard always calls runSplitQuery, which applies applyTemplateVariables again on those same targets (including expressions already rewritten by interpolateShardingSelector with __stream_shard__ and `| drop __stream_shard__`). applyTemplateVariables' contract is to inject ad-hoc filters from the third argument, and that injection appends matchers into each `{}` selector; it is not idempotent. With loki shard splitting on, every request that has ad-hoc filters therefore executes LogQL with duplicate matchers, and the second rewrite runs on an already sharded selector, which can produce invalid LogQL or a selector that does not match the stream selector used to fetch shard values. The updated test expects applyTemplateVariables five times (once up front plus once per shard group) but never passes filters, so this is untested. Interpolate once, and do not pass already rewritten targets back through filter injection.

findings.title: Empty expressions after interpolation are no longer removed
findings.body: Previously shard splitting interpolated first and then dropped targets whose expr was empty. The new code filters on query.expr before applyTemplateVariables, so a target whose expression is only a variable (for example `$query`) that resolves to `""` is kept. That empty target is then grouped, used for shard lookup, and sent to Loki. An empty query parse error fails the shard group and stops the split instead of skipping the target as before. Filter again after interpolation, matching the old order.
